dinkum-3.meaning: All facts kept: dates, offices, Walatowa Saturdays, $10 and "$2.50 service fee on top", tags, "a 15-foot (4.6 m) tree, say, needs two", Year 4 free permit with the fee, and the thinning rationale. Metric conversions are helpful colour.
dinkum-3.sense: "get first dibs" fits priority; "Year 4 kids" is the right Australian equivalent of fourth graders; "does the bush a good turn" and "patches of feed for the wildlife" carry forest health and forage correctly.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural plain Aussie: "have a proper read", "pop in the pass or voucher number", "skinny little trees". The constant "Chrissie tree" gets a little forced by repetition.
dinkum-3.register: A light, level-2 touch: mostly plain notice prose with "Chrissie", "first dibs", "heads up" sprinkled in; no swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Stays an informative public notice, friendly but businesslike: "Get in touch with us for current opening hours."
dinkum-3.flow: Reads smoothly: "That depends on the weather and how many there are, and people who can't cut their own tree get first dibs."
dinkum-3.variety: "Chrissie tree" is used for nearly every mention ("Chrissie tree permits", "pre-cut Chrissie trees", "a Chrissie tree permit for free", "cutting a Chrissie tree"), a noticeable tic.
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the permit notice: how to buy, where, cost, tag rules, kids' pass, forest-health pitch.

dinkum-4.meaning: Everything is there, including "$10 and non-refundable", "an extra $2.50 service fee", the tag rule, the Walatowa dates and "priority goes to people who can't cut their own tree".
dinkum-4.sense: "up for grabs" strains for permits that are sold, since it suggests free for the taking; otherwise terms fit.
dinkum-4.authenticity: Mostly natural, but "Fourth graders (Year 4 kids)" is an awkward gloss and "does the forest's health a favour" is a stiff blend.
dinkum-4.register: Lighter than A: largely the original wording ("It's important to have a careful read", "Visitors will also need") with "Chrissy" and "up for grabs"; a touch under level 2.
dinkum-4.tone: Keeps the notice tone: "Get in touch with us for current hours."
dinkum-4.flow: Readable, with some stiff joins: "Cutting a Chrissy tree also does the forest's health a favour."
dinkum-4.variety: Mixes "Chrissy tree" with "Christmas tree", so no single term is overused, though little slang overall.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All key facts kept. "Give us a ring for current hours" narrows "Contact us" to phoning; "cos it matters" is a reword of "It is important".
yarn-dinkum.sense: "first dibs", "skinny little trees" and "where wildlife can find a feed" fit; "the areas that do better for a thinning" strains.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Mostly natural ("pop in the pass or voucher number", "mind you"), but "cos it matters" tacked on is forced, and "Fourth graders" is left in US form.
yarn-dinkum.register: About level 2: "Chrissy", "first dibs", "Give us a ring", "does the bush a good turn"; no swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Mostly the notice tone, but "before you buy the permit, cos it matters" is a little flippant for a must-read instruction.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Mostly smooth, but "pick the areas that do better for a thinning" is ungrammatical and the "cos it matters" tag is a clunky join.
yarn-dinkum.variety: "Chrissy tree" repeated for every mention ("Chrissy tree permits", "pre-cut Chrissy trees", "a Chrissy tree permit for free").
yarn-dinkum.essence: Recognisably the same notice in every section.

dinkum-3.quote: And cutting a Chrissie tree does the bush a good turn, too.
dinkum-3.original: Cutting a Christmas tree also improves forest health.
dinkum-3.why: Chrissie is leaned on for almost every mention of Christmas tree; it reads as a tic rather than natural variation.

dinkum-4.quote: Chrissy tree permits will be up for grabs online
dinkum-4.original: Christmas tree permits will be available to purchase online
dinkum-4.why: Up for grabs implies free for whoever takes them; these are paid permits.

dinkum-4.quote: Fourth graders (Year 4 kids) with an Every Kid Outdoors pass
dinkum-4.original: Fourth graders with Every Kid Outdoors pass
dinkum-4.why: Bracketed gloss reads like a translation note rather than natural Australian.

dinkum-4.quote: Cutting a Chrissy tree also does the forest's health a favour.
dinkum-4.original: Cutting a Christmas tree also improves forest health.
dinkum-4.why: Clunky blend of idiom and the formal noun phrase.

yarn-dinkum.quote: Have a good read of the overview and the need-to-know info before you buy the permit, cos it matters.
yarn-dinkum.original: It is important to carefully read the overview and need-to-know information prior to purchasing the permit.
yarn-dinkum.why: Tacked-on tag is clunky and slightly flippant for a warning.

yarn-dinkum.why: Ungrammatical; an Australian would stumble on it.

summaries.dinkum-3: Accurate, light and natural; only the repeated "Chrissie" weakens it.
summaries.dinkum-4: Faithful and safe, but light and a little stiff in places.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Right weight, but a few forced or broken lines.
